# VECTA — Mandatory reference-first design benchmark
Date: 2026-11-11
Status: RESEARCH COMPLETE; visual direction NOT yet approved.

## RULE: no more auto-generated, brand-first SaaS-like wedding landing pages
The next VECTA design MUST be built by studying the specific verified references below.
It cannot be approved merely because it compiles or passes viewport tests.
Do not recycle the rejected MagicPath "Editorial 03 / Luxury" or "Director's Cut"
as the visual baseline. No giant VECTA wordmark as a substitute for real
photographic presentation, no red scribble-as-art-direction, no sentimental
wedding copy.

Ranking is editorial judgement about usefulness to VECTA, **not** verified
conversion rates or measured user testing.

## Top 10 verified live websites and concrete donors

### 1. BOTTEGA53 — https://www.bottega53.com/
- Direct inquiry: https://www.bottega53.com/contact
- Film: https://www.bottega53.com/film
- Search/filters: https://www.bottega53.com/search
- Why: real fashion-editorial wedding brand. Dense 3-column portfolio and short
  moving media, project names/venues, filtering by party/film/editorial/press,
  advanced inquiry including role, event date, guest count, location.
- VECTA donor: **entire visual/portfolio backbone and motion-in-grid**.
- Do NOT lift its sentimental philosophy, exact brand UI, imagery or code.

## Explicitly rejected or secondary
- Hafenliebe (https://www.hafenliebe-weddingphotography.com/) showed a
  **coming-soon** landing screen at the time of verification: not a
  multi-page funnel reference.
- Many Pinterest/Showit/Framer wedding templates: high-style mockups, not
  proven multi-page studio service funnels.
- A Fist Full Of Bolts (https://afistfullofbolts.com/) is useful as an
  auxiliary 35mm+Super8 editorial-journal reference, but not priority top-10.
- Norman & Blake is an auxiliary fine-art portfolio reference but smaller
  service funnel depth than the chosen set.

## 5 mandatory VECTA page patterns, derived from sources
1. **Bottega-style project-first entrance.** Real photos and occasional
   short silent loops lead. VECTA wordmark is legible, not a giant
   screen-filling substitute for content.
2. **Rich wedding case studies.** Proper wedding project pages with a
   curated multi-scene photo sequence, short film embedded if available,
   venue/year/format and clear related work. Never invent case studies.
3. **Categorized depth.** Projects; Photography; Wedding Films; About;
   Approach; FAQs; Journal; pages about genuine geographic services for
   Moscow/region only if useful and truthful.
4. **High-end service argument.** Clear process, collaboration with
   organizers, deliverables, coverage conditions, FAQs, controlled proof
   (only if substantiated), not empty marketing adjectives.
5. **Measured high-intent funnel.** Qualified request from any page:
   name/contact, event date/location, photo/video/combined, planner if any,
   context and optional budget band when useful; disclose data practices.
   Telegram handoff can remain an interim route but does not substitute a
   backend-confirmed lead.

## Important safeguards
- No change to existing approved Editorial Mosaic: one large + four small,
  same-size slots for photos/short muted video loops; final layout may live
  within a richer portfolio-first system, not necessarily be the entire site.
- Source photography/films belong to source owners; use for **study only**,
  not for VECTA portfolio/public site.
- Site screenshots alone do NOT prove conversion effectiveness.
- Never claim measured sales conversions for any source without metrics.
- For Russian launch, align actual service geographies/keywords, currency
  and relevant analytics to Yandex rather than copying foreign brands' SEO.
- Owner decides reference direction before changing production. New designs
  must cite concrete source URL + component behavior borrowed in code review.

Research sources: original websites, direct inner pages, 2026 industry
benchmark lists and designer's Bottega53 case study. 10/10 primary URLs were
retrieved by independent browser extraction on 2026-11-11.
